WEEK ONE
TOPIC:VALUES
PERIOD I: MEANING OF VALUES
DEFINITION
Value is the acceptable way of living considered as normal by a particular group of people. Values are also defined as the degree of importance an individual attaches to a particular thing. Values also mean the worth of a particular thing in monetary terms. Value refers to what a society regards as very important and is held in high esteem.
THE IMPORTANCE OF VALUES
- It helps individuals to make decisions.
- Value promote positive relationship among different people.
- Values promote peace and progress of the society.
- Values enable us to choose friends that share the same values.
- Values help to regulate people’s behavior.
- Values enable people to obey the rules and regulations of the country.
- Values prevent people from making mistakes.
Evaluation
- Define Value.
- What are the importance of values?
Period II
TOPIC: SOURCES OF VALUES
CONTENT:
Individuals acquire values through the agents of socialization. Socialization is the process by which individuals learn the values and culture of the society. These agents of socialization are sources of values. They are:
- Family: The family is the primary source of value. Children receive values from their parents.
- Peer Group: Children learn from  their peers
- School: The schools inculcate values in the children and students.
- Mass media e.g. Television, radio and newspapers.
- Religion: The churches and mosques teach values.
- Voluntary organizations e.g. red cross, girls guide, boys scout etc also teach values.
Factors That Influence Our Values
- Equality: Understanding that everybody has the same rights irrespective of their ethnic groups and gender.
- Honesty: Telling the truth, that is, meaning of what you say.
- Respect: Treating everyone including yourself with dignity and respect.
- Self - control: Being able to control your own actions.
- Responsibility: We should carry out our duties and must be responsible for our actions.
- Social Justice: We should treat people equally and fairly.
Values Clarification
- Being clear about our own values and beliefs helpus to make decisions that feel right to us.
- Value clarifications serve as a guide to achieve set goals in life.
- Values clarifications help us to become the kind of person we want to be and live the kind of life we want to live.
- Values clarifications prevent us from making mistakes in life.
- Values clarifications serve as a guide in our relationship with other people.
Evaluation
- Identify the sources of values.
- What are the factors that influence our values?
General Evaluation / Revision Questions
- What are the subjects that make up of social studies?
- Explain social and physical environments.
- Define socialization.
- Mention four agents of socialization.
- Define crime.

WEEK TWO
TOPIC:   CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES I
PERIOD I
CONTENT: MEANING OF RELIGIONS:
Religion is the belief in the worship of God. It can also be defined as is the belief in the existence of a supreme being called God who created the entire universe including plants, animals and human beings.
Types of Religions Institutions
- Christianity: Christianity is a religion that teaches about Jesus Christ. His followers are called Christians and they believe he is the son of God who came to the world to serve mankind. Christians make use of the Holy book called Bible. Their main day of worship is Sunday.
- Islam: Islam is the religion revealed through Prophet Mohammed in the Arabian city of Mecca. Muslims believe that Mohammed is the last of the Prophet and messenger of God. The teachings of Islam are contained in the Qur’an which is the Holy book of the Muslims. The Muslims main day of worship is Friday.
The Five Pillars of Islam
- Muslims believe that there is only one God and Mohammed is the messenger.
- Praying five times a day.
- Giving alms to the poor.
- Fasting during the month of Ramadan.
- Pilgrimage to Mecca at least once in a lifetime
African Traditional Religion (ATR)
African traditional religion refers to the original traditional beliefs and practices of the various people of Africa. African traditional religion forbids all evil practices including theft, murder, adultery, all forms of wickedness, deceit and cheating.
Evaluation Questions:
- Define religion.
- List and explain the various types of religions institutions.
PERIOD II
TOPIC: THE NAMES WE CALL GOD IN DIFFERENT COMMUNITIES IN NIGERIA.
CONTENT:
The Yorubas call God Olodumare or Olorun.
The Igbos call God Chineke or Chukwu.
The Edo people call God Osanobwa. The Hausa/Fulani call God Allah or Ubangidi.
The Efik people call God Abasi or Edidem.
The Benefits and Functions of Religious Institutions
- Religious institutions promote love, peace and friendship.
- They teach respect for God and for man.
- They provide rules and regulations which help to control the behaviour of their members.
- Religious institutions teach their members to shun all forms of evils and criminal activities.
- Religious institutions teach their members to believe that God can help them in times of trouble.
- Religious institutions provide explanations to some of the mysteries of life.
Similarities in the Lessons our Religion Teaches us.
- All religious institutions forbid lying, stealing, adultery and murder.
- They encourage their members to live holy life while on earth so that they will return to God in heaven after death.
- All religious institutions in the world require their members to submit totally to the will of God.
- Religious institutions especially Islam and Christianity teach that God is righteous and merciful.
Evaluation
- What are the benefits of religious institutions?
- Mention the names we call God in different communities in Nigeria.
General Evaluation / Revision Questions
- Define friendship.
- Highlight four factors that determine the choice of friends.
- List the agents of socialization.
- Identify five components of culture.
- Define family.

WEEK THREE
TOPIC: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES II
MARRIAGE I
PERIOD I:
CONTENT: MEANING OF MARRIAGE
Marriage is the legal coming together of a man and a woman as husband and wife. According to the bible, marriage was the first institution ordained by God. God created plants, animals and later created Adam and Eve as husband and wife and kept them at the Garden of Eden. It is marriage that joins a man and a woman to become husband and wife.
Evaluation Questions:
- Define marriage.
- Identify the first institution created by God.
PERIOD II
TOPIC: TYPES OF MARRIAGE
CONTENT:
- Monogamy: This refers to a marital relationship between a man and a woman i.e one husband and a wife.
- Polygamy: This refers to a marital relationship between a man and more than one wife.
- Polyandry: This refers to a marital relationship between a woman and more than one husband.
- Inter - Ethic Marriage: This refers to a marriage relationship between a man and a woman from two different ethnic groups, e.g when an Igbo man marries a Yoruba woman.
- Intra - Ethnic Marriage: This refers to a marital relationship between a man and a woman from the same ethnic group e. g when a Yoruba man marries a Yoruba woman.
- Christian Marriage: Christian marriage takes place in the church and is conducted by a Priest or a Pastor. Marriage vows are taken by the couple. There is also exchange of rings. A certificate is also given to the couple.
- Muslim Marriage: Muslim marriage is done according to the principles of the Holy Quran. Another name for Muslim marriage is Nikkah. It is conducted by a Muslim Priest in the house of the bride or Mosque.
- Court Marriage: Court marriage is performed in a court registry by a court registrar or a magistrate. Marriage vows are taken by the couple. There is also an exchange of rings and certificate is given to the couple. It is called ordinance marriage.
Purposes of Marriage
- Marriage is an important means of reproducing man in the society. Without marriage, the dead members of the society cannot be replaced.
- Marriage is for companionship between husband and wife.
- Marriage unites the families of both husband and the wife together.
- Marriage gives security to the woman and the children.
- It allows the husband and the wife to assist each other.
- A married man or woman is regarded as a responsible person in the society.
- Marriage provides a framework for the raising and training of the children.
- In traditional society, marrying many wives gives the man a high status.
Evaluation Questions:
- List and explain five types of marriage.
- What are the purposes of marriage?

WEEK FOUR
TOPIC: MARRIAGE II
PERIOD I:
TOPIC: THE CONDITIONS FOR MARRIAGE
CONTENT:
The conditions for marriage are as follows:
- Marriage is contracted between those who are not closely related.
- It is the man in most cases that approaches the girl and asks her to be his wife.
- The man and the woman inform their parents.
- Each family inquires into the family background of the other to know if the family is well mannered and does not suffer from any incurable diseases.
- A person often acts as an intermediary between the couple before wedding.
- The consent of the two is important before a marriage is contracted.
- Bride price is paid by the husband or family of the husband.
Evaluation Questions:
- Mention the conditions for marriage.
Period II
Topic: Effects of Lack of Readiness in Marriage Relationship
Content:
- It leads to separation and divorce.
- It causes to poverty.
- It often exposes the children to unnecessary abuse by either of the parent or outsiders.
- It prevents the cordial relationship between the parents and the children.
- It can force the female child to engage in pre-marital sex which may lead to unwanted pregnancy and sexually transmitted diseases e.g. HIV/AIDS etc.
- The children will be exposed to many dangers.
Challenges or Problems in Marriage
- Separation: Separation in marriage is when the couple is no longer living together. This could be as a result of misunderstanding and constant quarrelling between husband and wife.
- Divorce: Divorce occurs when the marriage has been dissolved with a legal document backing up the separation. This is the greatest challenge or problem of marriage.
- Quarrelling: A constant fight between the couple can lead to divorce.
- Economic instability: This occurs when the couple finds it difficult to meet the financial and needs of the family. The basic needs are food, shelter and clothing.
- Raising and proper upbringing of children: This is another problem parents face in marriage.
- Barreness: This is when the wife could not give birth to children. This could lead to divorce.
- Infidelity: Extra marital relationship by either of the couple can cause misunderstanding and divorce.
- Family disapproval: There will be a serious challenge if any of the family of the couple does not approve the marriage
- Interference by the members either the wife’s or husband family can cause misunderstanding between the couple.
- Death: The loss of either of the couple through death poses a great challenge to the family.
Solutions to Marital Challenges
- Forgiveness: Couple should be able to forgive each other whenever an offence is committed
- Tolerance: Husband and wife should learn how to tolerate each other weakness
- Trust: Couple should build their relationship on trust and mutual understanding
- Faithfulness: Couple should be faithful to each other
- Mutual Respect: Respect for each other reduces challenge in marriage and also promotes cooperation.
- Avoidance of intruder: Husband and wife should learn to settle their problems between themselves and avoid unnecessary interference from friends and relations.
- Good Counselor such as religious leader also help to solve marital challenges and problems
- Love: Love is the most important factor that promotes good marital relationship. Husband and wife should endavour to love one another.
Evaluation
- What are the effects of lack of readiness in marriage relationship?

WEEK FIVE
TOPIC: FAMILY AS THE BASIC UNIT OF SOCIETY
PERIOD I: ADVANTAGES OF LIVING TOGETHER IN FAMILY
CONTENT:
Family refers to those who are related by blood, marriage or law. The family is the smallest social unit of a society, it is the part through which a child comes into the world. A family is formed when a man and a woman through marriage agree to live together as husband and wife.
There are two common types of family in our society. These are the nuclear and the extended family. A nuclear family consists of a man, his wife and their children, while an extended family is made up of a man, his wife or wives, children and other relations like cousin, nephews, grandparents etc.
Advantages of Living Together in the Family
- Protection: It is the duty of the parents to protect their children from danger. The parents must ensure that they live in a safe environment.
- Unity: Living together in the family promotes the spirit of unity among members of the family.
- Provision of basic needs: The family is responsible for the provision of basic needs like food, clothes and shelter for the children.
- Education of children: The family creates opportunity for the children to receive formal education by sending them to school and paying their school fees.
- Good social behaviour: The family provides avenue for the teaching of acceptable cultural values by parents to their children.
- Happiness: The family provides happiness for the members of the family.
